'''Suicide Falls''' is the downward terminus of the [[Ditch]], a waterway in [[Sigil]] between the [[Lower Ward]] and [[Hive Ward]]. This is probably the easiest way to physically exit via the edge of Sigil for those without the power of flight.
Not quite a waterfall, water (and jumpers) that goes over the edge of [[Sigil]] simply disappears. As there's no turbulence common to waterfalls, the "falls" are eerily silent. Anyone who has looked over Sigil's edge has reported that outside of Sigil is simply ''nothing''.<ref name="pscssab58">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=58, ''Sigil and Beyond''}}</ref><ref name="pscssab59">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=59, ''Sigil and Beyond''}}</ref> As such, bodies are never recovered. The [[Harmonium]] sometimes say that missing youths must have "succumbed to the Falls' siren."
The terminus is actually a delta, with a collection of small islets dotting the waters. On one of these islets grows the [[Last Kiss Blossom]].

Its only standing structure, the '''Shattered Castle''', also known as the '''Shattered Keep''' and the '''Castle of the Supreme Throne''', was the [[divine realm]] of [[Cyric]], the Prince of Lies. Following the murder of the Goddess of Magic, [[Mystra]], the realm also became Cyric's prison, by the hands of fellow gods [[Lathander]], [[Tyr]], and [[Sune]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|74}} {{quote |[[Malik el Sami]]: "You shut yourself in the Shattered Keep—"
[[Cyric]]: "Castle of the Supreme Throne!"
Malik: "—and delude yourself into believing you play other gods like puppets. |Exchange between Malik and Cyric in a farm near [[Candlekeep]]{{Cite book/Crucible|149-150}} }} ==Cosmology== According to the [[Great Wheel cosmology]], the Shattered Castle was a realm within [[Cocytus]], the second layer of [[Pandemonium]], after Cyric retreated from his previous realm of [[Bone Castle]] in [[Hades]].{{Cite book/Ruins of Zhentil Keep/Campaign Book|113-114}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|17}} ==Geography== Much like the rest of Cocytus,{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|95}} the Supreme Throne was a barren realm where howling winds could drive mortals mad. Because Cyric was the enemy of all other faiths, the followers of any deity besides Cyric found their spells more difficult to cast on the plane. The Shattered Castle was a twisted and ruined fortress that first served as Cyric's seat of power, and as his prison afterwards. It was called the "Castle of the Supreme Throne" only by Cyric himself. ==History== According to a thrall captured by [[mind flayer]]s of [[Oryndoll]] beneath [[Andalbruin]], the Supreme Throne was originally established as a kingdom in the plane of [[Limbo]] by [[batrachi]] who had left [[Toril]] after around {{Yearlink|-31500}}. There, the deity called [[Ramenos]] once again changed the batrachi to serve his goals.{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|5}} The Shattered Castle was then moved by Cyric and brought to Pandemonium as he retreated to that plane after reading the ''[[Cyrinishad]]'' in the {{YearlinkName|1368}}.{{Cite book/Ruins of Zhentil Keep/Campaign Book|24-26}} Cyric, driven mad, abandoned Bone Castle in Hades and established his new realm in Cocytus as a twisted, ever-changing fortress, which served as his base from where he hatched his plans to conquer [[Toril]]. In the {{YearlinkName|1385}}, after Cyric murdered Mystra and triggered the [[Spellplague]], Lathander, Sune, and Tyr decreed that Cyric be imprisoned in the Supreme Throne for 1000 years.{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|159}} ==Inhabitants== The Supreme Throne was the home plane of [[chaos beast]]s, [[demodand]]s, [[howler]]s, and [[slaad]]i. It was also home to [[howling dragon]]s and [[chaos dragon]]s.{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|11}} Since its inception in Limbo, the realm was inhabited by [[batrachi]]. Among them was [[Bazim-Gorag]], the Firebringer.{{Cite book/Champions of Ruin|152}} ==Rumors & Legends== A rumor existed that seven black [[iron]] keys were required to free Cyric from his shackles within his prison.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|45}} ==Appendix== ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Limbo}} {{Pandemonium}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Locations in Pandemonium]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Fiendish planes]] [[Category:World Tree planes]] [[Category:Astral dominions]] [[Category:World Axis planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Lower Planes]]

It was a place of slime and mud. ==Geography== The plane was a vast swamp populated by [[hag]]s and twisted [[tree]]s. Few settlements existed in the place, built atop high stilts that kept constructions above the mud. However, since there was no solid ground underneath, everything eventually sank into the swamp. Objects thrown into the swamp were rumored to disappear into the mud for at least a century. For that reason, powerful [[artifact]]s were occasionally thrown in the swamp by someone desperate to remove them from the [[multiverse]] for a time. At the border with the Plane of Earth, a hill range known as the [[Mud Hills]] were constantly eroded by the Swamp of Oblivion and regenerated by the Plane of Earth. The border with the Plane of Water was known as the [[Silt Flats]], a muddy and sludgy region that marked the boundary between the swamp and the endless sea.{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|57}} ===Flora & Fauna=== Some of the few animals known to be found on this plane included [[leech]]es{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|84}} and enormous swarms of mosquitoes. ==Appendix== {{Incomplete}} ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Para-Elemental Planes]] [[Category:Inner Planes]] [[Category:Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]]

Who says a city is supposed to do something?'' | Migon the Sly<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/> }}
==Geography== Approximately {{SI|1000|mile|k|long=yes}} from the base of the [[Spire]],<ref name="MotP3e-p148_149"/> the town was located in a forest of abnormally large flora. In this forest, the [[gate]] to Arborea moved around, always invisible. Often, travelers looking for a way out of Sylvania's surrounding foliage would pass through the gate unknowingly and into Arborea.<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/>
==Government== Sylvania was governed by a group known as the Seven Spiritors. The Seven were spirits known to possess bodies of mortals for years or decades at a time in order to take a physical form, with most hosts volunteering themselves for the position. They were each known by a title that reflected their natures: Action, Knowledge, Pain, Passion, Reflection, Rest, and Thought.<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/>
==Notable Locations== * The [[Sensate Embassy]], a pyramid of petrified wood that contained lodging and offices for members of the [[Society of Sensation]], as well as a hall for combat and revelry.<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/> * The Acropolis, a temple dedicated to the whole [[Olympian pantheon]].<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/> * The Elven Living Temple to [[Arvandor]], which was carved into a massive living banyan tree.<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/> * The Dipping Dragon, an inn and tavern made in the shape of a dragon. The upper floors were mounted on a pivot that moved up and down to make it appear that the dragon was drinking from a pond.<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/> * Thunderhouse, a festhall.<ref name="PPO2e-poster"> {{Cite book/A Player's Primer to the Outlands|Postermap}}</ref> * Greyfalcon's, an inn.<ref name="PPO2e-poster"/>
==Inhabitants== The population of Sylvania was split evenly between [[humans]], [[elves]], and [[bariaur]].<ref name="PPO2e-p24"/>
==Rumors & Legends== Sometime prior to the creation of his own [[divine realm]],<ref name="poly119-p22">{{Cite polyhedron/119/Forgotten Deities: Finder Wyvernspur|22}}</ref> [[Fermata]],<ref>{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|14-15}}</ref> the [[Faerûnian pantheon|Faerûnian power]] [[Finder Wyvernspur]] was rumored to have been seen in Sylvania in the company of the goddess [[Tymora]].<ref name="poly119-p22" />

The '''Syndicate of Terror, Extortion, Assassination, and Larceny''' (or '''STEAL''') is an evil multiverse-spanning criminal organization. They're rivals to the good-aligned [[Golden Vault]].
== Background Information == * STEAL is part of a long tradition, primarily from spy media, of evil organizations with tortured acronyms. Examples include FOWL (Fiendish Organization for World Larceny, ''Darkwing Duck''), HIVE (Hierarchy of International Vengeance and Extermination, ''Teen Titans''), SPECTRE (Special Executive for Counter-intelligence, Terrorism, Revenge, and Extortion, ''James Bond''), VENOM (Vicious, Evil Network of Mayhem, ''M.A.S.K.''), and VILE (Villains' International League of Evil, ''Carmen Sandiego'').

[[File:DitchMap.png|right|300px|Ditch map]] The '''Taker's Lock''' is an artificial canal system about halfway down the length of the [[Ditch]], roughly half a mile from the [[Bridge That Spans Worlds]].
== History ==
A portion of the Ditch was once a shallow trickle, prohibiting most vessels from entering further into Sigil, a desirable proposition due to the increased ability to trade further upstream. The [[Fated]] funded the construction of a series of watertight locks which would elevate ships, allowing them to go up and downstream at will.
Of course any ship wanting to make use of the Lock must pay the Fated a toll. It also provides an excuse for a "customs station" where the Fated can search cargo to levy import taxes, or confiscate any illegal material. The Fated also pay to keep a battalion of [[Harmonium]] present in case ship captains refuse to pay or submit to inspection.
In a rare example of a [[faction]] openly working with a [[guild]], Takers insist that any loading and unloading at Sigil's docks can only be done by accredited workers from the [[Guild of Teamsters]] (which the Takers will provide for a fee). Teamsters, in turn, pay a "registration fee" to remain on the "sanctioned worker's list."
== Background Information == * Although the text implies that the Locks are in main part the Ditch itself, the Lazz illustration suggests it's part of a side tributary, leaving the main Ditch unobstructed.

{{Quote|''Has reality got you down? Tired of the everyday, humdrum, commonplace happenings of life on the [[Prime Material Plane]]? Want to ''really'' get away from it all? Then step right up for the chance for adventure out of the ordinary ... ''way'' out of the ordinary ...''
''Tales of the Outer Planes is an anthology of short adventures set throughout the many [[Outer Planes]] for use with the AD&D<sup>®</sup> [[Manual of the Planes 1st edition|Manual of the Planes]]. Some of gaming's best designers have contributed adventures to this set, which include scenarios set in the [[Seven Heavens]], [[Olympus]], the four [[Elemental Planes]], the [[Nine Hells]], and the [[Astral Plane|Astral]] and [[Ethereal Plane]]s. Tales of the Outer Planes is a perfect collection for powerful characters who have it too easy at home and are looking for new challenges. Many of the most fearsome monsters are even more dangerous on their own planes—can you take them on and live to tell the tale?''
''These adventures can be inserted as a "change of pace" in an existing campaign, or can be the foundation of an entire new set of adventures. Either way, Tales of the Outer Planes will be sure to open up a whole new frontier for AD&D<sup>®</sup> game players everywhere.''}}
==Description== The module provides pre-generated mini-adventures to introduce player characters to extra-planar worlds either as stand-alone campaigns or part of on-going campaigns. There are 11 adventures in the outer realms and 17 lair adventures that focus on creatures from an outer plane.
==Contents== * How to Use Tales of the Outer Planes
The book also contains a number of adventures, set in the [[Planes]]: * Prime: [[Tales of the Outer Planes/A Simple Deed, Well Rewarded|A Simple Deed, Well Rewarded]] * Ethereal: [[Tales of the Outer Planes/Castle at the Edge of Time|Castle at the Edge of Time]] * Air: The Brewing Storm. Adventurers must secure the release of an imprisoned [[janni]] amir in the [[Elemental Plane of Air]]. * Water: The Voyage of the ''Nereid''. Adventurers are invited to explore an ancient temple in the [[Elemental Plane of Water]]. * Fire: Through the Fire. Adventurers must snatch an artwork made of living fire from an [[efreet]] in the [[Elemental Plane of Fire]]. * Earth: [[Tales of the Outer Planes/The Missing Kristal|The Missing Kristal]] * Astral: Into the Astral Plane. Adventurers are called on to rescue a [[wizard]] from [[githyanki]] in the [[Astral Plane]]. * Seven Heavens: An Element of Chaos. Adventurers are asked by a [[deva]] to remove a corrupting presence in [[Mount Celestia]]. * Olympus: [[Tales of the Outer Planes/A Friendly Wager|A Friendly Wager]] * The Abyss: [[Tales of the Outer Planes/The Sea of Screams|The Sea of Screams]] * Nine Hells: To Hell and Back. A demon asks adventurers to retrieve an artifact from the [[Nine Hells]].
Finally, the book offers some short adventures in the manner of the [[Book of Lairs]]. Two of them have indications they're set in the Realms. * [[Archon]]s * [[Babau]] * [[Berbalang]] * [[Dao]] * [[Farastu]] * [[Githyanki]] * [[Githzerai]] * [[Grey slaad]] * [[Ildriss]] * [[Kuei]] (in [[Kara-Tur]]) * [[Marid]] * [[Modron]]s * [[Planetar]] * [[P'oh]] and [[General Ox]] ([[ch'ien]] are used) * [[Ultrodaemon]]s

The '''Temple of Hermes''' was a religious building in the [[Temple District]] of [[The Lady's Ward]] in the city of [[Sigil]]. It was located near the spireward edge of the ward.
The temple was dedicated to the power [[Hermes]]. The assistant underpriestess was [[Mad Moll]]. The building contained a [[portal]] to [[Mount Olympus]], and every morning carts of [[Arborea]]n fruits were transported through the portal to the city.

'''Terras''' is a world on the [[Prime Material plane]].
During the ''War of Lies'', a lich raised an unimaginably large army of the undead. It's said that no dead remained who had not been raised.
A pair of priests opened a rift to the [[Astral Plane]], sending the entire army through.
That army now floats endlessly in the Astral as the [[Bonecloud]].<ref name="gtta80">{{b|Planescape|A Guide to the Astral Plane|pdf=17287|page=80}}</ref>

{{Unrelated}} {{Creature | image = <gallery> Tertians.jpg|2e Tertian-1e.jpg|1e </gallery> | caption = | name = Tertian | size5e = | type5e = | subtype5e = | alignment5e = | challenge5e = | refs5e = | size4e = | origin4e = | type4e = | subtype4e = | alignment4e = | refs4e = | size3e = Large | type3e = [[Outsider]] | subtype3e = | alignment3e = Always [[lawful neutral]] | challenge3e = 16 | refs3e = <ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17">{{Cite web enhancement/The Modrons|16-17}}</ref> | size2e = Large | alignment2e = [[Lawful neutral]] | refs2e = <ref name="PSCS">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/Monstrous Supplement|16-20}}</ref> | size1e = Large | alignment1e = [[Lawful neutral]] | refs1e = <ref name="MM21e-p91">{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|91}}</ref> | patron deity = [[Primus]]<ref name="MotPWE3e-p2">{{Cite web enhancement/The Modrons|2}}</ref> | vision = [[Darkvision]]<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> | activecycle = Any<ref name="PSCS"/> | diet = | lifespan = | location = [[Mechanus]]<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> | language = [[Modron language|Modron]], [[Abyssal language|Abyssal]], [[Auran]], [[Celestial language|Celestial]], [[Infernal language|Infernal]], [[Sylvan]], [[Telepathy]]<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> | subraces = | climate = Any<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> | terrain = Any land<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> | height = {{SI|12|ft}}<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> | length = | wingspan = | weight = | skincolor = | haircolor = | hairstyles = | feathers = | eyecolor = | build = | distinctions = | based = | first = [[Monster Manual II 1st edition|''Monster Manual II'' 1{{st}} edition]] }} '''Tertians''' were the second-most powerful type of hierarch [[modron]]s.
==Description== Tertians were very tall humanoids, with a height of {{SI|12|ft}}. They had a prehensile tail that acted as a third arm, at the tip of which was a growth that was similar to a [[mace]]. A tertian had a ring of horns that encircled their hairless head.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" />They appeared muscular and carved as if from a dark [[onyx]].<ref name="Dung144">{{Cite dungeon/144/Diplomacy|68–85}}</ref>
==Combat== If forced into combat, a tertian will use a combination of innate abilities, spells, tail and fists.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" />
==Abilities== Like all hierarch modrons, tertians had the innate ability to duplicate the effects of ''[[clairaudience]]'', ''[[clairvoyance]]'', ''[[command]]'', ''[[dimension door]]'', ''[[teleport without error]]'', and ''[[wall of force]]'' spells at will.<ref name="TGMM">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|126}}</ref> Tertians were able to cast [[arcane]] spells as well as [[divine]] spells from the [[Law domain|Law]], [[Protection domain|Protection]] and [[War domain|War]] domains. Tertians were immune to all effects that influenced the mind, all psionic-based attacks and had a resistance to acid, cold and fire.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" />
==Society== They acted as judges, judging and sentencing both [[modron|modrons]] and non-natives.<ref name="MM21e-p91" /><ref name="PSCS" /><ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" /> Nine tertians existed, with eight of them reporting to the [[secundus|Secundi]], and the final one reporting to [[Primus]] himself.<ref name="MM21e-p91" /><ref name="PSCS" /><ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" />
==Ecology== Tertians were able to communicate telepathically with any sentient creature within {{SI|405|mi|k}} and could see in [[darkvision]] up to {{SI|60|ft}}.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p16-17" />

An endless ocean with numerous islands, it was the headwaters of the River [[Oceanus]].<ref name="MotP3e-p138-141" /><ref name="PoC2e-p63-64">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|63-64}}</ref>
==Description== The layer's infinite ocean was peppered with islands with white [[sand]] beaches and warm lagoons. Some islands were populated and supported towns and communities of various sizes.<ref name="PoC2e-p63-64" /><ref name="MotP3e-p138-141" />
The weather on Thalasia varied from cold and windy to warm and calm. The seas could be rough when the weather was windy, but the islands generally enjoyed a mild tropical climate.<ref name="PoC2e-p63-64" />
==Cosmography== [[Yggdrasil]], the World Ash, extended its branches to this layer, as well as all other layers of Elysium, except [[Belierin]].<ref name="PC-LB2e-p6">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|6}}</ref>
==Notable Locations== * [[Portico]], an island town near where the Oceanus flowed into [[Belierin]] and a common stopping point for travelers.<ref name="PoC2e-p63-64" /> * [[Ro Stau]], realm of [[Seker]], appeared as a sunlit pleasure hall at a river bank when it manifested here.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|90}}</ref> * [[Selkies' Grotto]], realm of [[Surminare]], goddess of [[selkie]]s. An underwater cave complex that was often visited by [[Deep Sashelas]] and [[Trishina]].<ref name="PoC2e-p63-64" />
==Rumors & Legends== Some islands in Thalasia were rumored to be inhabited by great heroes from the [[Prime Material plane]]. They could only be reached by travelers who sought the aid of those heroes, and only after certain conditions were met, determined by the heroes' individual legends.<ref name="PoC2e-p63-64" /><ref name="MotP3e-p138-141" />

{{DEFAULTSORT:Great Modron March, The}} {{Book | image = The-Great-Modron-March-cover.jpg | caption = | code = TSR2628 | title = The Great Modron March | author = [[Monte Cook]], [[Colin McComb]] | editor = [[Michele Carter]] | cover_artist = [[Randy Post]] | inter_artist = [[Randy Post]], [[Adam Rex]], [[Ray Nadeu]] | cartography = [[Rob Lazzaretti]] | typography = [[Angelika Lokotz]] | publisher = [[TSR, Inc.]] | released = October 1997 | reprinted = | type = Adventure | binding = | pages = 128 | languages = | realm year = | game_edition = 2 | isbn10 = 0786906480 | isbn13 = 978-0786906482 | series = | preceded_by = | followed_by = | source = | Roll20number = 17302 }} '''''The Great Modron March''''' is a Planescape<sup>®</sup> AD&D 2nd-edition adventure module.
{{Quote|'''''THE NEXT MARCH WASN'T DUE FOR ANOTHER 189 YEARS. TRY TELLING THAT TO THE MODRONS!'''''
''On a regular schedule, the Great Modron March spills out of [[Mechanus]], and the lawful automatons files their way around the Great Ring. No one knows why they do it, but everyone stays out of their way - because when the [[modron]]s march, they'll walk right over a berk who doesn't know enough to move aside.''
''But this March has started decades before it was supposed to begin, and that's even more of a mystery. Caught unprepared, the planes shudder under the modrons' collective footsteps - and even the modrons themselves seem a little out of sorts.''
''The Great Modron March anthology features 11 adventures for characters ranging from 1st to 10th level, as well as new information about the modrons of Mechanus. Each adventure can be played separately or linked together to form an extended campaign. The modron procession touches every [[Outer Plane]] in turn - and it isn't always welcome. On their unswerving path, the clockwork creatures will destroy celestial towns, be attacked by evil knights intent on using modron parts in foul experiments, and lead characters onto the deadly plains of the [[Abyss]] and into the famous prime-material labyrinth of [[Undermountain]]. Without help, they'll be lost in the swirling chaos of [[Limbo]] or even fail to complete the March entirely.''
''And along their route, every blood on the planes seeks the answer to the most important question: Why have the Modrons abandoned their normal, lawful schedule to march years before they're due? ''}}

[[File:Ladys Ward map.jpg|thumb|right|400px|A map of the Ward]] '''The Lady's Ward''' is one of the six wards of [[Sigil]]. It's home to the city's upper classes, being the most prestigious of the wards. It is also home to the headquarters of the [[Harmonium]], [[Mercykillers]], [[Fraternity of Order]] and [[Doomguard]] factions. But in the [[World Tree cosmology]], it was said to be part of [[Heliopolis]] and had the [[River Isis]] pass through it, the former of which was a [[plane]] shared by all members of the Mulhorandi pantheon. ==Geography== Thoth's Estate had a wide variety of terrain throughout it, though the World Tree's conception of it was said to be marshy. In the areas where the River Ma'at passed through, it had deserts and swamps vying for dominance of the riverbank. ==Notable Locations== * The Great Wheel cosmology described this realm as having a number of villages and towns that dotted the banks of the River Ma'at, which were inhabited largely by the [[petitioner]]s of Thoth. These were mere extensions of a nearby city, referred to as Thebestys, one of the largest towns in the Outlands that wasn't also a [[gate-town]]. One could find both libraries and schools here, an expression of Thoth's role as a deity of knowledge.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|115}} * In the World Tree cosmology, there was likewise a city named Thebestys and several smaller villages. * The '''Great Library''', the hallowed halls where Thoth stored his accumulated knowledge, stood at the center of Thebestys. It was rumored that almost any answer one could want to search for was housed within the library, its vast collection rivaled only by the [[House of Knowledge (plane)|House of Knowledge]]. Thoth would gladly allow scholars to research within it, welcoming all who sought knowledge, but one would have to search through its immense collection of [[scroll]]s. ==Inhabitants== The petitioners that lived in this realm carried out mundane lives. In addition to the petitioners, one could find [[crocodile]]s and crocodile-like creatures in the River Ma'at. ==Appendix== ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Outlands}} [[Category:Divine realms]] [[Category:Locations in the World Tree planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]]

'''Tieflings''' (TEEF-ling) are mortals who have unknown planar ancestry, typically (and largely accurately) assumed to be from among the creatures of the [[Lower Planes]]: [[tanar'ri]], [[baatezu]], [[gehereleth]]s, [[yugoloth]]s, and others. Often distrusted as a result, tieflings feel a strange mixture of pride and shame with their identity. They're referred to as ''[[plane-touched]]'', although that term also includes [[aasimar]] and [[genasi]].
The planar ancestry is typically more than a generation back -- half-[[tanar'ri]] such as the [[cambion]]s and [[alu-fiend]]s do not count as tieflings, for example.
== Appearance == No two tieflings look alike, each betraying some aspect of their ancestry: Cloven hooves, claws, patches of scale, or even just a constant shadow across their eyes.
A tiefling's appearance can generally be split into three legacies, based on the origins of their fiendish blood:
=== Abyssal Tiefling ===
With fiendish origins in [[Pandemonium]], The [[Abyss]], or [[Carceri]], these are the more chaotic tieflings, and typically have [[tanar'ri]]c blood. They'll tend to have horns, fur, tusks, and particular scents.
=== Chthonic Tiefling ===
With fiendish origins in [[Carceri]], [[Hades]], and [[Gehenna]], these are the more neutral tieflings. Their blood may come from a [[night hag]] or a [[yugoloth]]. They may have a cadaverous appearance, the unearthly beauty of a succubus, or other features in common with their parent.
=== Infernal Tiefling ===
With a fiendish parent from [[Gehenna]], [[Baator]], or [[Acheron]], these tieflings have lawful ancestry. Their fiendish parent may be one of the [[baatezu]]. They tend to have horns, spines, tails, golden eyes, and the smell of sulfur or smoke.
Although tieflings tend to be a largely [[planar]] phenomenon, there are some worlds with a rather high preponderance of tieflings, such as [[Toril]], a world with much magic and planar travel.
In approximately [[119 YFHR]], [[Asmodeus]] enacted a ritual on Toril, ensuring all tieflings in the world would have the "blood of Asmodeus" -- effectively rewriting all tieflings such that their ancestry could be traced to him. This was a gambit to make him the "racial god" over the world's tieflings, allowing him to ascend to full godhood rather than merely being a [[Lord of the Nine]].
Accordingly, for decades afterward, Toril's tieflings all had a similar appearance, owing to their shared Infernal ancestry: primarily reddish skin, a tail, and horns. However, tieflings of other ancestry (and appearance) continued to exist in other worlds and planes.<ref name="scag118">{{Forgotten Realms|Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|page=118}}</ref>
: ''A table for randomly generating tiefling appearance traits can be found on {{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=80}}.''
== Background Information ==
* "Tiefling" comes from the German "tief," meaning deep or low, a reference to their Lower Planar origins. * The 119 YFHR year for Asmodeus' ritual was determined by taking the publishing year of the Lost Gods trilogy (1997) -- a crossover series covering Forgotten Realms, Greyhawk, and Planescape -- and its date in Dale Reckoning (1368 DR). Planescape books published in 1997 take place in [[129 YFHR]]. The date of Asmodeus' ritual took place in 1358 DR, ten years earlier, so subtracting 10 from 129 gives us a date of 119 YFHR. * Of course, this assumes time flows at the same rate in Toril and the Planes, which may not be the case: there's a difference of approximately 150 years between FR's 1st Edition (1357 DR) to the most recent of 5th Edition as of this writing (Acquisitions Incorporated, 1496 DR)

[[Sigil]] breaks down its timekeeping in its own particular way, given that it's not a prime world and cannot rely on the planet's rotation. It's come up with a system sometimes called Sigil Standard Time, or SST, which has become popular with planewalkers. == Time of Day == Sigil is not on a spinning ball, so cannot rely on to what degree the planet is facing the system's sun in order to tell time. However, the sky does gradually get lighter and darker. The brightest part of the day is '''peak''', and the darkest, at the opposite time of day, is '''anti-peak'''. A day works out to about the same length as on other prime worlds, and is divided into 24 hour segments. However, all time is measured by proximity to peak, with BP (before peak) and AP (after peak). Primes should note that PM and AP match fairly well, but AM and BP work in opposite directions. Also note that, for partial hours (e.g. 4:30) the 30 minutes is not always after the hour. They typically do not have numbers on them, making it easier for Sigil's many cosmopolitan races to read. They are, at least, divided in 24-hour increments. It can be assumed that minutes and seconds are also used in Sigil, but for most people it's likely a rough guide and not anything precise. == Seasons == As the city is not on a planet with an axial tilt, it has no defined seasons. While the [[Ditch]] sometimes freezes over enough that it could be walked across, it's on no regular schedule that could be called "winter."{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 137|page=14-17}} One of the only signs of the passage of seasons in Sigil is the [[Grand Gardens]] in [[The Lady's Ward]], which changes appearance matching the seasons one might experience on a prime world.{{b|D&D|Dungeon Masters Guide 2|pdf=144108|page=195}} == Years == Most Cagers use relative terms -- a few years ago, a dozen years ago, a thousand years ago -- but the [[Fraternity of Order]], of course, has its own system. When exact timekeeping is needed the Guvners measure time by how long their current [[factol]] has been in their position. Currently they're measuring the Year of Factol [[Hashkar]]'s Reign, and previous to him, time was measured as the Year of Factol [[Lariset]]'s Reign, and so on back in time. : See also: [[Timeline]] : ''AD&D 2nd Edition [[Planescape]] books were released between the [[126 YFHR|126th Year of Factol Hashkar's Reign]] (1994) and [[130 YFHR]] (1998), with one in-game year advancing for each real-world year. Assuming this continued, the current year would be [[{{#expr: {{CURRENTYEAR}}-1868}} YFHR]].'' == Other Timekeeping == No alternate methods of timekeeping -- such as days of the week, or months -- have ever been officially defined. Even Guvners typically measure a year's passage with terms like "the 87th day of the 127th Year of Factol Hashkar's Reign". When a Cager says "I'll deliver your shipment in a week," that could be anywhere from five to ten days. == Chronomancy == Access to [[Temporal Prime]] is completely blocked in Sigil by the [[Lady of Pain]], who does not personally like [[chronomancy]]: possibly because the Lady herself has some form of time-manipulation ability and doesn't want anyone else interfering. [[Chronomancer]]s who reveal their powers in Sigil become pariahs, and invariably and quickly disappear, forever.{{b|D&D|Chronomancy and the Multiverse|page=7-8}} == Background Information == * Ante-meridiem (AM) means "before midday," so while linguistically it's similar to "before peak," it's not intended to represent the number of hours before midday; just noting hours occurring in the pre-noon half of the day. * While no official attempts have been made to define days of the week or months of the year, a number of fans have made their own efforts, based on things like the Wards of Sigil, the factions, or the Outer Planes. == References == * {{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|page=12}} * {{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=53}} [[Category:Sigil]]

This page contains a timeline of events from '''Planescape''' and associated media.
There is no standard system of measuring years in Sigil beyond the current year of [[Factol]] [[Hashkar]]'s reign (YFHR), so that standard will be used here. Events preceding Hashkar's reign will be represented with BFHR (Before Factol Hashkar's Reign). Other timekeeping methods may also be covered where appropriate.

== After the War == After the publication of {{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299}}, timeline data is scarce. Particularly with the change in editions, it's uncertain when various entries from 3rd edition and 4th edition are meant to take place, other than "after the Faction War."
This is exacerbated by 5th edition, which was a semi-reboot, with some evidence that places it post-Faction War (e.g. the existence of the [[Mind's Eye]]), and some that seems to suggest the Faction War never happened -- or hasn't happened yet (e.g. the various missing [[factol]]s, including those killed in the War, are back in charge).
In absence of other evidence, DMs may assume the standard set during 2nd edition -- that one publication year is equivalent to one year in-universe -- is still in place, making the current year, [[{{CURRENTYEAR}}]] equivalent to [[{{#expr: {{CURRENTYEAR}}-1868}} YFHR]].
== Other Events == * There's a yearly gala in the [[Lady's Ward]] at the [[Palace of the Jester]], called the "[[Day of Grace]]." Each year it's hosted by a different family who, of course, try to outdo the previous year's celebration.<ref name="fw12">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=12}}</ref> Grace is held on the first day of the year (at least, on Guvner calendars).<ref name="poly127-23">{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 127|page=23}}</ref> * The [[Guildhall Ward]] has a quarterly street festival and celebration called [[Harmony]], covering the final few days of the month, once every three months.<ref name="fw20">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=20}}</ref> * The [[Festival of Doors]], once a spiritual event, has become an excuse for raucous celebration, particularly among the upper class. [[Cavefire wine]], a rare commodity from the [[Shadowfell]], is essential to proper celebration, but also includes [[ice apples]] and [[glitterbeast]]s.<ref name="dmgii210211">{{b|D&D|Dungeon Masters Guide 2|pdf=144108|page=210-211}}</ref> * After [[Vecna]]'s defeat in [[132 YFHR]], Sigil celebrates with a week-long festival, sure to be enacted on a regular basis.<ref name="dvd150">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=150}}</ref>
== Note == * Much like the AD/CE and BC/BCE system, there is no "year zero." When Hashkar becomes Factol, that is the beginning of [[1 YFHR]]. As such, be careful with subtraction for past events: an extra number must be added to the numerical value. For example: 500 years before [[130 YFHR]] would be [[371 BFHR]], not 370.

{{Plane | image = Tir na og reduced res.png | caption = | name = Tir na Og | othernames = The Land of Youth | symbol = Outlands.png | demonym = | natives = | languages = | basicrefs = <ref name="OHG-p68-75">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|68-75}}</ref> | type-GW = Realm | shape-size-GW = | gravity-GW = | time-GW = | morphic-GW = | element-energy-GW = | alignment-GW = {{Alignment grid|off|off|off|off|on|off|off|off|off}} | magical-GW = | layers-GW = | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = the [[Outlands]] | refs-GW = <ref name="OHG-p68-75" /> | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = | settlements = yes | based = [[wikipedia:en:Tír na nÓg|Tir na nOg]] (Irish) | usethe = | useon = }} '''Tir na Og''' was a large and beautiful realm in the [[Outlands]]. It was considered one of the largest shared realms in the [[Outer Planes]]. According to the [[Great Wheel cosmology]], the realms of [[Silvanus]] and [[Oghma]] were located within its vast territory, as well as the realms of many other [[deity|deities]].<ref name="OHG-p68-75" />
==Geography== The realm was an expanse of meadows and [[oak]] groves that extended among hills and woods. The landscape was dotted with obelisks, cairns, and circles of standing stones, from which ancient [[magic]] often emanated.<ref name="OHG-p68-75" />
There were no large cities in Tir na Og; only villages and small settlements. The countryside also displayed single homes and farms.<ref name="OHG-p68-75" /><ref name="PPO2e-p31-32">{{Cite book/A Player's Primer to the Outlands|31-32}}</ref>
==Defenses== The realm's inhabitants fiercely defended their freedom and neutrality. If visitors were caught violating any of those principles, a strong measure of defense employed by some of the powers in the realm was to unleash the [[Wild Hunt]] upon the transgressors.<ref name="OHG-p68-75" /><ref name="PPO2e-p31-32" />
==Notable Locations== Several realms were located within Tir na Og, separated by between around 3 and 18 days' travel from one to the next.<ref name="PPO2e-p31-32" /> Notable realms included: * The [[Deep Forest]], realm of [[Silvanus]].<ref name="FA2e-p145">{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|145}}</ref> * The [[House of Knowledge (plane)|House of Knowledge]], realm of [[Oghma]].<ref name="FA2e-p131">{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|131}}</ref> * The [[Pinnacle]], realm of [[Dunatis]].<ref name="OHG-p70">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|70}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== Tir na Og was inhabited mainly by [[petitioner]]s and former citizens of the [[Prime Material plane]] who sought a life of peace and quiet. Most of the realm's inhabitants lived outside of its settlements, roaming the hills or living among the forests.<ref name="OHG-p68-75" />

{{Plane | image = | caption = | name = Tomb Tapper Tomb | othernames = The Tomb | symbol = | demonym = | natives = | languages = | basicrefs = <ref name="UD-p179"/><ref name="MoF-p83"/> | type-GW = | shape-size-GW = | gravity-GW = | time-GW = | morphic-GW = | element-energy-GW = | alignment-GW = | magical-GW = | layers-GW = | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = | refs-GW = | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = [[Demiplane]] | shape-size-WT = {{SI|2|mile|k}} in diameter, {{SI|0.5|mile|k}} high | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = <ref name="UD-p179"/> | inhabitants = | creatures = | deities = | locations = | organizations = | settlements = | usethe = | useon = }} The '''Tomb Tapper Tomb''', also known as simply '''The Tomb''',<ref name="MoF-p83">{{Cite book/Monsters of Faerûn|83}}</ref> was a [[demiplane]] filled with innumerable magic treasures with an entry [[portal]] somewhere in the [[Buried Realms]] region of the [[Lowerdark]] beneath [[Anauroch]].<ref name="UD-p179">{{Cite book/Underdark|179}}</ref> It comprised one of the richest—and best defended—hoards in all of [[Faerûn]].<ref name="MoF-p83"/>
==Description== The tomb itself was an enormous {{SI|2|mi|k}} wide and {{SI|0.5|mi|k}} high chamber lit by a dim gray light. Gravity was nonexistent in this space and the flow of time was erratic and unpredictable relative to the outside world. The air was said to be stale and poor in quality. Magic followed a similar detriment, with even the most basic of spells becoming incredibly difficult to cast when within the demiplane. Tomb tappers were faced with the opposite effect and thereby their magic was enhanced as long as they were within this realm.<ref name="UD-p179" />
Slowly floating through the gravity-free void were over a dozen castles that doubled as vaults for magic items stolen from all across [[Faerûn]] by the tomb tappers. Each of these castles were ringed by thousands of orbiting boulders. These boulders could be manipulated with spellcasting to create temporary bridges between fortresses.<ref name="UD-p179" />
There were so many [[magic items]] present in the vaults that not even a [[portable hole]] or [[bag of holding]] could contain them all.<ref name="UD-p179" />
==Geography== The tomb was located in a demiplane created by the very same [[Netherese]] [[arcanist]]s that created the titular [[tomb tapper]]s. The only way to access the tomb was through a portal deep within the Lowerdark beneath the deserts of Anauroch. The portal would move up to {{SI|12|miles|k|long=yes}} to a new location every one to ten days, regardless of if that location was connected to a cave system or not, leading to it potentially being embedded in solid stone until its next change in position.<ref name="UD-p179" />
==History== As of the mid-to-late 14{{th}} century [[DR]], the Tomb remained little more than a rumor among [[adventurer]]s of the surface, and was said to be some sort of temple in which the tomb tappers kept all of their stolen magic items.<ref name="MoF-p83"/>
==Inhabitants== The tomb contained a wide variety of powerful beings that would not let their treasure be taken easily. Treasure vaults themselves were often guarded by a dozen or more [[tomb tapper]]s alongside various undead and constructs. All creatures guarding the vaults were incredibly hostile and would attack living intruders on sight, often calling for reinforcements from other castles within the tomb.<ref name="UD-p179" />
The most powerful being in the demiplane was the [[demilich]] known as the [[Keeper of Thaal]]. The Keeper was often seen with a small gathering of various undead under his command created from the deaths less fortunate adventurers, including the likes of [[lich]]es and ghosts. The tomb tappers unerringly followed his command, so it was suspected that he was their true master.<ref name="UD-p179" />

{{Quote|''I just find Torch so much more relaxing than [[Sigil]]. The lava, the explosions, the boils, the blood marsh—it just does a body good.''|Bantrice the Potter<ref name="APPttO-p25" />}}
==Description== The gate-town was divided into two parts. The lowest part was the most dangerous part of Torch. The impoverished and desperate inhabitants lived here. Occasionally, the marsh flooded this section of the gate-town, bring waves of disease and a species of [[killer frog]]s, poisonous snakes and [[giant leech]]es. The wealthiest and most powerful inhabitants of Torch made their homes in the upper slopes, divided into three sections called Karal, Maygel and Dohin. Connected by towering bridges, the upper part of Torch was walled of from the lower town. A popular past-time of the residents of the upper sections was standing on the bridges and watching the struggles of the residents of the lower town.<ref name="HB-WG-p43">{{Cite book/Hellbound: The Blood War/War Games|43}}</ref><ref name="APPttO-p25" />
===Gates=== Floating about {{SI|100|ft|long=yes}} in the air, the Gate to Gehenna appeared as a large dark red gemstone. Flying into the gate was the safest course of action, but some brave, or foolhardy, individuals attempted to pass through the gate by dropping down from one of the volcanic spires. Local legend stated that there was a hidden second gate to Gehenna found in the marsh surrounding Torch.<ref name="APPttO-p25" />
==Geography== [[File:Tir fo Thuinn Map.png|thumb|300px|''A map showing the Torch's location in relation to other gate-towns and the River Ma'at.'']] Torch was built on the slopes of several towering volcanic spires, formed by cooled magma. Some of the spires were still active, occasionally producing inflammable gases and lava flows. The constant light from the ever-present lava was how the gate-town came to be called Torch. The town and the spires were surrounded by a large march filled with water the color of blood.<ref name="APPttO-p25" />
There was a roughly a distance of three to eighteen journeying days between Torch and the [[River Ma'at]].<ref>{{Cite book/A Player's Primer to the Outlands|5}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== Due to the ever-present light, Torch never slept. The inhabitants of this gate-town were some of the most dangerous individuals in the Outlands. They were known for their greed and vicious, violent temperament. They held the belief that everything in the Outlands, and beyond, was theirs by right and did not hesitate to do whatever was necessary to possess it. Thankfully, they spent so much time robbing each other than raids on other gate-towns were rare.<ref name="APPttO-p25" />
The gate-town was home to several thieves guilds. The largest six were<ref name="APPttO-p25" />:
* Gray Orb * Kindred of Yoj * Severed Hand * Brotherhood Janko * Tiamat's Chosen * Fire Lords
The thieves guilds were in constant conflict, each desiring to corner the black market. Full-on brawls in the streets were not uncommon. The closest they had to a neutral meeting ground was the [[Festhall of the Falling Coins]],<ref name="APPttO-p25" /> which was run by a [[Toril]]ian [[wizard]] named [[Badurth]].<ref>{{Cite book/Hellbound: The Blood War/War Games|45}}</ref>
==Government== The closest thing Torch had to a local government was the Council of All. It was, in theory, a council of the inhabitants of the town. Meeting were held in the ruins of an abandoned arena. In reality, the meetings often devolved into large fights, with the council being run by the most wealthy, and powerful, inhabitants.<ref name="APPttO-p25" />

'''Toril''' is the primary inhabited world found within [[w:c:spelljammer:Realmspace|Realmspace]] on the [[Prime Material plane]]. As an incredibly magic-rich world by Prime standards, it's full of portals and magics that enable planar travel. In terms of prime representation in the planes, Toril is probably the most common homeworld.
Its primary continents include ''Faerûn'' and ''Zakhara''.

== Portals ==
Many portals on Toril were constructed using a powerful spell called "Worldwalk" and some kind of permanency magic, which makes for permanent keyless gates. This ''should'' be impossible for mortals. It's possible on Toril only; the same magic won't work elsewhere.
The following portals are known to link to Toril:
* Between [[Alfheim]] ([[Ysgard (plane)|Ysgard]]) and Evermeet * Between [[Arvandor]] ([[Arborea]]) and Evermeet * Between Undermountain and the [[Lower Planes]] * A window in [[Harbinger House]] looking out over Waterdeep.<ref name="hh52">{{b|Planescape|Harbinger House (book)|alt=Harbinger House|pdf=17277|page=52}}</ref> * The [[Seafarer's Arch]] in the [[Ditch]] links to sewer pipe from the Underdeep leading into the Trackless Sea<ref name="poly137-15">{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 137|page=15}}</ref>
An ancient kingdom called Netheril had plenty of portals, but with the destruction of that empire, most portals and their locations have been lost, if any are still active.
The [[World Serpent Inn]] caters to primes from Arabel on Toril, and some claim is actually ''in'' Arabel, so its entrances may be portals, or it may exist in both places simultaneously.
